details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has issued a warning that while tokenized financial markets offer efficiency benefits, their rapid expansion and increasing interconnectedness could magnify traditional financial stresses. The IMF highlighted risks such as fire sales, liquidity runs, and contagion, calling for clearer legal and regulatory frameworks, along with stronger integration between tokenized and conventional financial systems. The report noted that tokenized equities exhibit higher volatility and lower liquidity compared to their traditional counterparts.
title: IMF Warns Tokenized Markets Could Amplify Financial Stability Risks

details: Bitcoin's price experienced a notable drop on October 8th, falling below the $81,000 mark. This decline was primarily attributed to growing fears of potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and substantial outflows from US-listed spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). The broader sell-off also affected altcoins, with Ethereum and XRP facing even sharper percentage losses, indicating a general decrease in risk appetite within the crypto market.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $81,000 Amid Macro Headwinds and ETF Outflows

details: Recent weaker-than-expected US jobs data for September has led to a significant reduction in the market's expectation for an October interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. This softer macroeconomic outlook is generally seen as positive for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, as it implies a less aggressive monetary policy stance. However, elevated Treasury yields and rising oil prices continue to pose potential headwinds for the broader market.
title: Weak US Jobs Data Dims October Fed Rate Hike Bets, Supports Crypto

details: The Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed to advance in the US Senate on September 15, falling short of the 60 votes required for procedural passage. This setback, largely due to disagreements over ethics provisions rather than the core market structure framework, represents a significant hurdle for establishing comprehensive federal cryptocurrency regulation in 2026. The focus for crypto rules may now shift more towards actions by regulatory agencies like the SEC and CFTC.
title: US Senate Fails to Pass CLARITY Act, Stalling Comprehensive Crypto Regulation
